# Directory server sources: every candidate, terms, verdict (2026-10-06)

Branch `feature/portal-directory`. Evidence: research agent (WebSearch/WebFetch + curl with the honest UA
`NxeonDirectoryResearch/1.0 (+https://nxeon.cloud; abuse@nxeon.cloud)`, max ~3 requests per site, nothing blocked
was bypassed; raw notes in `research-raw.md`) plus my own single verification requests to Klei (below). WebFetch
summarises pages with a small model, so quotes marked (WF) should be re-read by a human before relying on them.
This is an engineering risk assessment, not legal advice.

Verdicts: **USE** = documented and clearly permitted. **NEEDS-OWNER-REVIEW** = accessible, no explicit prohibition
found but no explicit permission either (or terms unreadable): adapter may exist but is default OFF until the owner
records a reviewer. **DO-NOT-USE** = forbidden, blocked (Cloudflare/403/robots), credentialed, or dead.

## Bottom line
- **Minecraft (Java + Bedrock): no permitted bulk discovery source exists.** Every server-list site either forbids
  copying, disallows its listing pages in robots.txt, sits behind a Cloudflare challenge, has no readable terms, or
  only offers per-server vote/owner APIs. None was scraped. The implemented path is **owner-submitted listings
  verified by a token in the server's own MOTD** (or A2S name / DNS TXT), enriched with our own Server List Ping /
  RakNet ping. Plus Nxeon-hosted servers (paid + free Minecraft tier), which already list.
- **Steam GetServerList stays the bulk source** for the ~30 Steam-master families (already approved by the owner).
- **New adapter, default OFF: Klei DST lobby list** (NEEDS-OWNER-REVIEW).
- **New source, default OFF: owner submissions** for every game (the only route for the ~15 no-list games).

## Table

| Source | Games | What it is (URL) | Terms quote / evidence | Terms URL | Verdict | Why / what was built |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Steam IGameServersService/GetServerList | 30 Steam-master families | Bulk list, key in prod env | "you will store the Steam Data in a country (or countries) identified in your privacy policy"; "limited to one hundred thousand (100,000) calls ... per day" (spec, 2026-10-05) | https://steamcommunity.com/dev/apiterms | USE (owner approved: `directory_steam_terms_reviewed_by`) | Existing. 38,079 rows in prod today across 28 games. Enable: `directory_src_submitted_enabled=true` + `directory_src_submitted_reviewed_by=<name>`. |

Prober stores sanitized MOTD + version. |

## What is enabled vs needs sign-off
Nothing new is enabled. All new sources ship default OFF:
- `directory_src_submitted_enabled` + `directory_src_submitted_reviewed_by` (owner submissions; the portal form says "isn't open yet" while off)
- `directory_src_klei_enabled` + `directory_src_klei_reviewed_by` (DST)

**Incident.** Every fresh Minecraft Bedrock deploy failed provisioning with `game port 19132/udp never opened ... ECONNREFUSED`, on every node and plan. The container started, logged `Server started.`

**Root cause.** Since BDS 1.26.50 Mojang's default `transport` in server.properties is `nethernet` (WebRTC: one dual-stack TCP signalling socket on `server-port`, UDP negotiated per client), not `rakn

**Version matrix** (fresh data dir, throwaway VM; "RakNet ping" = unconnected ping to the published UDP port answered with a pong):

| BDS | default transport | with `TRANSPORT=raknet` |
|---|---|---|
| 1.26.45.1 | raknet: UDP 19132/19133 open, ping OK | same, ping OK |
| 1.26.50.5 | nethernet: TCP 19132 only, no UDP, ping fails | UDP open, ping OK (logs a TRANSPORT TYPE ERROR notice) |
| 1.26.51.1 | nethernet, same | UDP open, ping OK (notice) |
| 1.26.52.3 | nethernet, same | UDP open, ping OK (notice) |

Mojang download URLs that exist (2026-10-06): 1.26.40.8, 42.1, 43.1, 44.3, 45.1, 50.5, 51.1, 52.3. Not verified with a real game client (only the server side); the 50+ builds print a notice saying Net

**Fix.** `lib/bedrock-version.ts` is the single place: `BEDROCK_KNOWN_GOOD_VERSION` (1.26.52.3) and `BEDROCK_TRANSPORT` (raknet). `applyBedrockSetup` (called from `buildGameSetupScript`) resolves `VER

**Existing servers.** The container env bakes `VERSION=LATEST` and itzg re-resolves it on every container start, so every restart upgrades to the newest Mojang build; today that is harmless (their ser

**How to bump the pin safely.** Change the one constant `BEDROCK_KNOWN_GOOD_VERSION`, after first running a throwaway Bedrock server on the new build with the exact flags (`-e TRANSPORT=raknet -p 1913

- **Multi-line descriptions:** a line item `description` may contain `\n`. The first line is the headline; the rest are smaller muted sub-lines (HTML `.dsub`, PDF 9pt muted). Everything is escaped. `i
- Tests: `test/invoice-logo.test.ts`.

## Portal server directory overhaul + owner-submitted listings + Klei DST source (2026-10-06, branch `feature/portal-directory`)

The customer-portal directory (`/dashboard/directory`) was the old flat, client-filtered list of every row. It now has the same information architecture and the SAME data layer as the public v2 pages (`lib/directory-query.ts`: SQL paging + one cached facet GROUP BY, Nxeon-hosted merge, live blocklist re-check, liveness), drawn in the dashboard's own style. No logic is forked: URL filter state, the factual fallback line and the pager maths moved to the pure, client-safe `lib/directory-view.ts`, which the marketing hub (`app/nxm/_data/directory-hub.ts`) now imports too (it re-exports `readFilters`/`qs`/`factualLine` unchanged).

**Routes** (all `requireUser()`, `noindex`):
- `/dashboard/directory`: hero with real counts, search (`?q=`) and region (`?region=<slug>`) cross-game results; sections: Your servers (listing state per server), Favourites, Hosted on Nxeon, Browse by game (art + counts + playing), Near you (geo header / offline geoip, never stored), Browse by region (continents + top countries), Most players now, Newly listed, attribution.
- `/dashboard/directory/games`: every GAME_FAMILIES key, 0-server games included.
- `/dashboard/directory/<game>` and `/<game>/<region>`: region tabs + country chips with counts, URL-synced search/players/sort (`router.replace`, no history spam; plain GET form without JS), Nxeon-hosted pinned on page 1, 24 per page server-side, empty states with nearest regions, "more games like this".
- `/dashboard/directory/server/<id>`: connect address + copy, `steam://connect` for Steam rows, save, players/freshness ("Checked" only when our probe answered), map/version/slots/source, about (owner text, sanitized MOTD, or the factual line), similar servers. When it is the customer's OWN server, the game panel's Public Directory card is rendered inline (same actions, ownership enforced in `lib/actions-game-control.ts`).
- `/dashboard/directory/favourites`: saved servers resolved live; ones that left the directory show "not listed right now" from the stored snapshot; copy-all.
- `/dashboard/directory/list`: "List your server": each Nxeon server with its Public Directory card, the free MC server link, and "A server hosted elsewhere" (submissions, below).

**Code:** `lib/directory-portal-data.ts` (own servers, favourites, art), `lib/directory-portal-core.ts` (favourite/submit/verify/remove rules with the user id passed in, every query scoped by it), `lib/actions-directory.ts` (thin `"use server"` wrappers: `requireUser()` + rate limits + audit), `components/nx/directory/{DirBits,DirClient,GameListView,SubmitClient}.tsx`. The old `components/nx/DirectoryView.tsx` was deleted (`lib/directory-portal.ts` kept for its tests).

**Schema (additive, applied by promote's `prisma db push`, no data loss):** `DirectoryFavourite` (userId + PUBLIC directory id, unique per user, cap 200, name/address snapshot) and `DirectorySubmission` (owner submissions), plus the two User relation fields.

**Owner-submitted listings (source `submitted`, default OFF).** The only permitted way to list servers for games with no usable public list, Minecraft above all (no Minecraft list site permits republishing: see `/root/agent-notes/portal-directory/SOURCES.md`). The owner adds an address, gets `nxeon-<10 hex>`, and proves control by putting it in the MOTD (Java SLP / Bedrock RakNet), in the server name (A2S games) or in a DNS TXT record `_nxeon-verify.<host>` (any game, hostname addresses; re-verify every 30 days). Each Verify click sends ONE status query (or one DNS lookup), 6/min per account; hostnames must resolve only to public IPv4 (`resolvePublic`, SRV honoured for Java). The newest verified claim on an address wins. Verified rows go through the normal provider pipeline (`lib/directory-ingest/providers/submitted.ts`: dedupe vs Nxeon and other sources, blocklist, prune); removing a submission deletes its row at once. Switch on: Settings `directory_src_submitted_enabled=true` and `directory_src_submitted_reviewed_by=<who approved the policy>` (admin Directory > Sources lists it automatically). While off, the portal form is disabled with an honest note.

**Minecraft status enrichment.** `lib/directory-ingest/mc-status.ts` is a hardened SLP + RakNet client (public IPv4 only, ports >= 1024, 2.5 s timeout, 256 KB reply cap, advertised hostname in the Java handshake so virtual-hosted networks answer, player names never read). The prober (still OFF in prod, still only on a `NXEON_DIRECTORY_PROBE=1` box) now uses it for `slp`/`raknet` rows and stores the MOTD (sanitized by `lib/directory-text.ts`: formatting codes, invisible/bidi chars, URLs, invites, IPs, emails and domains removed, 280 chars) as `description` plus the reported `version`.

**Klei DST lobby source (`klei`, default OFF, NEEDS-OWNER-REVIEW).** `lib/directory-ingest/providers/klei.ts` reads the 4 public `lobby-v2-cdn.klei.com/<region>-Steam.json.gz` files the game client uses (verified 2026-10-06: ~1.8 MB gzip each, ~3.1k open dedicated servers in ap-southeast-1 alone), hourly, sequentially, keeping only dedicated, passwordless, not friends/clan/LAN-only servers; no mods or Steam ids stored. Klei publishes no terms for these files (only a second-hand, unverified staff remark that third-party tools are welcome): the owner confirms with Klei and records `directory_src_klei_reviewed_by` before `directory_src_klei_enabled=true`.

**Other fixes in passing.** Steam attribution in the portal now shows the Valve logo (when `public/brand/steam-logo.svg` exists) and no longer says "Nxeon checks each one directly" while the prober is off. `GamePublicListing`'s preview chip said "Minecraft" for every game; it now takes an optional `gameLabel` (omitted = no chip). React keys use the public id (the entry `key`, `x-<first 10 of a cuid>`, collides because cuids share a timestamp prefix).

**Tests:** `test/directory-portal-v2.test.ts` (pure: URL state, pager, factual line, sanitizer hostile cases, SLP/RakNet parsers incl. oversize frame, resolver incl. mixed public/private A records, submission parsing/verification with fakes, submitted candidates, Klei parser) and `test/directory-portal-db.test.ts` (throwaway DB via `DIRECTORY_TEST_DATABASE_URL`: favourites and submissions scoped per account, takeover, closed-by-default, ownServers isolation). Known pre-existing failure, unrelated: `test/directory-phase1-db.test.ts` "sweep: off by default..." expects 88 Steam calls but main's commit 8830922 (unfiltered 9th request per game) makes it 99; the default suite skips this DB-only test.
EOF
cat >> docs/DIRECTORY-SOURCES.md <<'EOF'

- **Minecraft / Bedrock:** re-verified: still no list site whose terms permit republishing (minecraftservers.org has a no-copy clause; minecraft-server-list.com disallows /servers/ in robots.txt; planetminecraft.com and findmcserver.com are behind Cloudflare challenges; others have no readable terms and only vote APIs). Not scraped. Built instead: owner submissions verified by a MOTD / A2S-name / DNS TXT token (source `submitted`, default OFF) and hardened SLP/RakNet enrichment. Full table: /root/agent-notes/portal-directory/SOURCES.md.
- **dst:** Klei lobby CDN `lobby-v2-cdn.klei.com/<region>-Steam.json.gz` verified live (one request per file). AMBER: no published terms. Adapter `providers/klei.ts`, default OFF, needs `directory_src_klei_reviewed_by`.
- **Every game without a list** (terraria, palworld, satisfactory, factorio, corekeeper, arkasa, necesse, nightingale, eco, armareforger, fivem, plutonium*, ...): owner submissions with DNS proof (or A2S name where the game answers A2S).
EOF

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

input.message:
## Portal server directory overhaul and server sources for all games

The portal directory is rebuilt with the same structure and data layer as the public v2 pages. For Minecraft there is still no source we're allowed to copy from. I didn't scrape anything. Instead I built owner-submitted listings, where the owner proves the server is theirs. All new sources ship switched off. Nothing is deployed or merged.

**Branch:** `feature/portal-directory`, worktree `/tank/nxeon-wt-portaldir`. Four commits on top of `main`:
- `e203b03597`: shared filter/pager module `lib/directory-view.ts` (the marketing hub now uses it, behaviour unchanged) and two new tables.
- `7e71682c77`: the portal overhaul, owner submissions, and hardened Minecraft status queries.
- `19ba910f00`: tests, a Don't Starve Together source, honest Steam credit line, small fixes, docs.
- `d1dc5394a7`: removed an unauthenticated server-action export that the existing auth guard test caught.

**Screenshots:** `/root/agent-notes/portal-directory/screens/`, 13 views at 1440 and 390 px. All views returned 200 with no horizontal scroll and no console errors except one missing flag image (`/flags/ir.png`), which falls back to a placeholder.

### Part 1: the portal
- **Home `/dashboard/directory`:** real counts, search, and these sections:
  - your own servers with their listing status;
  - favourites;
  - Hosted on Nxeon;
  - a game grid with art, counts and players;
  - near you;
  - continents and countries;
  - most players now and newly listed.
  - Adding `?q=` or `?region=` turns the home into a cross-game results list.
- **Per game and per region** (`/<game>`, `/<game>/<region>`): region tabs and country chips with counts, search/players/sort kept in the URL, Nxeon servers pinned first, 24 per page loaded from the database, honest empty states. There's also `/games` listing every game.
- **Server detail `/server/<id>`:** copy address, Steam connect link for Steam servers, save, players, how fresh the data is, map, version, slots, source, and similar servers nearby. On the customer's own server it shows the same listing card as the game panel.
- **Favourites:** stored per account (new `DirectoryFavourite` table, max 200). Servers that left the directory show as "not listed right now".
- **List your server `/list`:** the customer's Nxeon servers with their listing toggles, plus a form to submit a server hosted elsewhere.

### Part 2: sources

| Source | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Steam server list | USE (already approved) | Existing; 38,079 rows across 28 games in prod today |
| Owner submissions (new, all games) | Needs your sign-off (off) | The owner puts a token in the MOTD, the server name, or a DNS TXT record; one check per Verify click, public addresses only |
| Our own Minecraft Java and Bedrock status queries | USE, enrichment only | Hardened; the background checker stores the MOTD and version |
| Klei Don't Starve Together lobby list (new adapter) | Needs your review (off) | Public files, checked with one request each; ~3,100 open servers in one of 4 region files; no published terms |
| minecraftservers.org | DO-NOT-USE | Its terms forbid reproducing or copying the site |
| minecraft-server-list.com | DO-NOT-USE | robots.txt blocks its server listing pages |
| planetminecraft.com, findmcserver.com | DO-NOT-USE | Behind a Cloudflare challenge |
| minecraft-mp.com, minecraftpocket-servers.com | DO-NOT-USE | Vote APIs only; the second site's terms page returned 403 |
| topg, minecraft.buzz, namemc and 5 other list sites | Needs your review, nothing built | No terms found and no list API |
| mcsrvstat, mcstatus.io | USE, enrichment only | Not used; we query servers ourselves |
| Minetrack server list | Licence fine (MIT) | Only 2 servers, not worth building |
| Vintage Story, TruckersMP | Needs your review | Existing adapters, still off |
| FiveM, Palworld, Arma Reforger, GameTracker | Needs your review | No usable source found; these go through owner submissions |
| BattleMetrics, Factorio, Mojang featured servers | DO-NOT-USE | Blocked, needs a personal login, or no API |

The full table with exact quotes and URLs is in `/root/agent-notes/portal-directory/SOURCES.md`. Quotes came via a summarising fetch tool, so they're worth a human re-read.

### What's on versus needs your sign-off
Nothing new is switched on. To open each one:
- **Owner submissions:** set `directory_src_submitted_enabled` and `directory_src_submitted_reviewed_by` (approves the policy). Until then the portal form is disabled with a note saying so.
- **Don't Starve Together:** check Klei's position, ideally by asking them, then set `directory_src_klei_reviewed_by` and `directory_src_klei_enabled`.
- **Background server checker:** still off in prod; the new MOTD and version storing only runs inside it.
- **Steam logo:** you need to supply the official logo at `public/brand/steam-logo.svg`; Steam's terms ask for it.
- **Steam credit line:** it no longer claims "Nxeon checks each one directly" while the checker is off.

### Part 3: tests
- **New pure tests** (`test/directory-portal-v2.test.ts`): 17 pass.
- **New database tests** (`test/directory-portal-db.test.ts`): 5 pass, against a throwaway Postgres. They prove a customer can only read, change or remove their own favourites and submissions.
- **Existing directory tests:** 157 of 158 pass. The one failure (`test/directory-phase1-db.test.ts`, "sweep: off by default…", expects 88 Steam calls, gets 99) is already broken on `main`. It comes from commit 8830922, which added a 9th request per game. The normal suite skips this database-only test, so the baseline never caught it. I left it alone and suggested a separate task to fix it.
- **Typecheck:** `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- **Full suite:** not run cleanly. Free memory never reached 12 GB during a 30-minute wait, so your rule ruled it out. Before I applied the rule, one full run happened by accident while about 9 GB was free. It flagged only the export issue fixed in `d1dc5394a7`, but I didn't save its failure list. Instead I ran 51 targeted test files: everything that scans the source tree or touches the directory, the server query code or the auth guards. That's 828 tests with 10 failures, all in the 46-name baseline, none new.

The dev server and throwaway Postgres are stopped and deleted.

### Deploy steps
1. The schema change is additive only: two new tables (`DirectoryFavourite`, `DirectorySubmission`) and their links on `User`. The normal `prisma db push` in `promote-production.sh` applies it with no data loss.
2. Merge, then `deploy-staging.sh` followed by `promote-production.sh`. A `next build` hasn't been run because of the memory limits, so the staging build is the first full build.

### Risks
- **First full build is on staging.** Typecheck passes, but nothing has been built end to end yet.
- **Shared component change:** the listing card's preview chip used to say "Minecraft" for every game. It now hides the chip unless a game name is passed, so the game panel shows no chip there.
- **Directory checks run from the web server:** owner Verify clicks (rate-limited to 6 a minute per account), as did the old portal page's live counts.
- **Detail-page timing:** a server can be hidden by the live competitor blocklist up to 60 seconds after it's added, because of caching.
- **Cosmetic:** the mobile home page is long (about 8,000 px).
- **Worktree setup:** `node_modules` in the worktree is a real folder of links into prod's, except the database client, which is a local copy generated there. Prod's own files were never touched.
